rationale: U04f (lifecycle expired-context fix) closes the follow-on gap this pin's earlier transition (U04e's function rename) did not touch: AttachRefUnderLifecycle's refs SHARED acquire, taken AFTER fn returns but still under the lifecycle EXCLUSIVE lock, used to reuse the caller's ctx — sized only for the lifecycle-lock acquire above fn, seconds — even though fn can legitimately run for the whole ~15-minute create-poll window. The first brief refs contention hit after that window would then fail immediately on the already-elapsed deadline instead of retrying, leaving fn's already-started child live with no reference held. The fix gives that acquire its OWN fresh, RefAcquireTimeout-bounded context, detached from ctx via context.WithoutCancel. The pin now checks for that fresh context directly instead of the old ctx-reuse literal, so it polices the invariant that actually matters (a live, correctly-bounded context at acquire time), not just a name.
evidence: services/host/lease/ordering.go: `refCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), RefAcquireTimeout)` then `rl.AcquireShared(refCtx)`, replacing the prior `rl.AcquireShared(ctx)`

rationale: U04f (supervisor/lifecycle reliability fixes) hardens the teardown journal's read-modify-write two ways beyond the bounded-0600-file property this pin already checked: the write itself moved from a bare os.WriteFile(tmp, ...) to writeFileAtomic (a unique per-call os.CreateTemp name, same directory, plus rename — closing the same fixed-temp-name collision surface writeFileAtomic's own doc explains), and the whole read-modify-write cycle is now serialized ACROSS PROCESSES by withTeardownJournalGuard's flock, because an orphan sweep and a session's own teardown are frequently two different pix-host invocations racing the same journal path, and a unique temp name alone only stops one writer's rename from landing half another's data — it does nothing about two readers each reading the prior lines before either has appended. Both are genuinely new invariants, not a renamed literal, so the pin's checks now cover the flock-guarded call and writeFileAtomic's unique-temp-plus-rename shape directly instead of the old inline os.WriteFile call.
evidence: services/host/workflow/launch/reap.go: `return withTeardownJournalGuard(path, func() error { ... return writeFileAtomic(path, ..., 0o600) })`, guarded by `syscall.Flock(int(f.Fd()), syscall.LOCK_EX|syscall.LOCK_NB)`; services/host/workflow/launch/atomic.go: `writeFileAtomic` via `os.CreateTemp(dir, filepath.Base(path)+".tmp-*")` + `os.Rename(tmpPath, path)`
